covariates.description: Day-ahead forecast of load in the Commonwealth Edison (COMED) zone in MW — the zone whose price is the target.

rationales.rationale: COMED day‑ahead load is broadly above recent levels (horizon mean +0.3 sd and +1.4 sd versus the most recent 24‑step window overall), suggesting a sustained positive pressure on price across the full 1–24 window.

System load forecast is elevated across the horizon (horizon mean +0.3 sd and positive phase departures versus recent), supporting a general, moderate upward contribution to price throughout the window.

COMED day-ahead load is strongly elevated relative to recent and seasonal norms, especially across the daytime peak (steps ~6–18 show the largest +1.0–+1.5 sd seasonal departures and horizon mean ~+0.5 sd); given zone demand directly lifts zonal price, expect a strong positive adjustment concentrated in those peak hours.

System-wide day-ahead load is modestly above recent norms (horizon mean ~+0.2 sd, ~+0.4 sd vs the last 24 steps) and runs up end-to-end; a consistent, moderate positive pressure on price across the whole window is warranted.

COMED (in‑zone) day‑ahead load is above recent levels (horizon mean ≈ +0.4–+0.5 sd) with small same‑phase departures early then clear, sustained positive departures of ~+0.7–+0.8 sd through roughly steps 7–17 and tapering afterward. Because this is an in‑zone demand signal and is strongest mid‑window, expect a strong upward push in the mid horizon (7–17: ++) and a milder upward effect as departures decline (18–24: +); early hours show little same‑phase uplift so are left at 0.

PJM-wide day‑ahead load is elevated over the horizon (horizon mean ≈ +0.5 sd) with same‑phase departures rising to ~+0.9–+1.1 sd in the early‑to‑mid window and remaining positive through the mid‑late horizon. Higher system demand tends to lift zonal price, but the signal is diffuse and the target‑only base likely captures some of it; therefore apply a mild upward adjustment across the daytime/mid horizon (steps 6–18).

COMED (in-zone) day-ahead load is clearly above recent and seasonal norms (horizon mean ~+0.4 sd and same‑phase departures peaking around +1.3–+1.5 sd in the mid window), so expect a moderate upward lift in the early and late steps (1–6 and 19–24: +) and a strong upward push through the daytime peak (7–18: ++) where zone demand most directly lifts price.

PJM system load is modestly elevated on the horizon (horizon mean ~+0.1 sd and an end-to-end upward run ~+0.88 sd) with positive same‑phase departures through the day; this should exert a broad but mild upward pressure on zonal price relative to the target-only base, not strong enough to warrant a ++.

COMED (in-zone) day‑ahead load is clearly above typical across the horizon (horizon ~+0.4 sd) with the strongest same-phase positive departures concentrated in the mid-window (steps ~12–18 reach ~+0.5–+0.9 sd), implying a strong upward push in that mid span and milder upward support at the earlier and later steps.

PJM system load is modestly elevated on the horizon (small positive departures vs recent and a positive end-to-end run), which provides a broad but not large upward pressure on zonal price across the full 1–24 window.

COMED (in‑zone) day‑ahead load is clearly above recent levels (horizon mean ≈ +0.4 sd and +1.3 sd versus the most recent 24‑step window) with the strongest same‑phase positive departures concentrated in the daytime hours. Expect a moderate upward push in the early hours (1–5: +), a strong upward effect through the daytime peak when zone demand is highest (6–18: ++), and a milder positive support as departures taper later in the window (19–24: +).

PJM-wide day-ahead load is modestly elevated across the horizon (horizon mean ≈ +0.3 sd, small positive same‑phase departures and an end‑to‑end uptick). This diffuse, consistent positive demand signal is likely to raise zonal price relative to a target-only base but is not extreme, so apply a mild upward adjustment throughout 1–24.

adjusted.rationale: Fixed joint judgments call for a mild-to-moderate upward tweak overall. Steps 1–5 have a low base (mean ≈ 15.2) and weaker covariate support, while steps 19–24 show stronger positive covariate departures and a higher base (mean ≈ 33.6). A uniform +3.0 $/MWh (≈0.22 of the target SD = 13.82) balances the stronger late-window upside without overstating the uplift in the low early-hour base.

Both covariates give a strong daytime upward signal (COMED ≈ +0.9 sd, system ≈ +0.5 sd) and the base across 6–18 is already elevated (mean ≈ 34.9). Apply a clear, substantive uplift of +8.0 $/MWh (≈0.58 of the target SD) to reflect the pronounced mid‑day demand-driven lift signaled for these peak hours.

Expect a moderate upward push in the early hours (1–5: +), a strong upward effect through the daytime peak when zone demand is highest (6–18: ++), and a milder positive support as departures taper later in the window (19–24: +).

adjusted.rationale: Both covariates here are judged to push price up (early hours moderately and late hours mildly). The steps in this group include a mix of a lower early-morning base (steps 1–5 mean 15.21) and a higher late-window base (steps 19–24 mean 33.63). I choose a single moderate uplift of +4.0 price units (≈0.29 target‑sd) as a compromise that honors the positive judgment throughout the group while balancing the smaller early‑hour signal and the stronger late‑window support.

Both covariates push upward with stronger in‑zone demand during daytime (comed ≈+0.9 sd, system ≈+0.5 sd) and the base in this span is elevated (steps 6–18 mean 34.87, ≈+0.4 sd). I apply a substantive daytime uplift of +7.0 price units (≈0.51 target‑sd) to reflect the strong ++ comed influence reinforced by the system+ signal.

rationales.rationale: Local COMED day‑ahead load is well above its recent window (horizon mean +0.4 sd and ~+1.3 sd vs the last 24), and same‑phase seasonal departures are strongly positive through much of the horizon (particularly steps ~9–18); this is a clear, consistent upward pressure on COMED zonal price that supports a strong (++ ) upward adjustment across the full 1–24 window.

PJM system load is moderately elevated (horizon mean ~+0.3 sd, modestly above the recent 24), and same‑phase departures are generally positive; this provides a consistent but smaller upward effect on price, supporting a + adjustment across 1–24.

adjusted.rationale: Both covariates push up (COMED strong, system mild). COMED is substantially above its recent and same‑phase levels (~+0.7 sd of its recent), with consistent positive departures through much of the horizon, and system load adds a smaller positive contribution (~+0.2 sd). Given the current target scale (sd ≈ 13.82) and a base forecast horizon mean of ~30.5, I apply a clear but not extreme upward correction of about 0.51 sd (7.0 price units). This raises the forecast mean to roughly 37.5, reflecting the strong zonal load signal tempered by only modest system‑level elevation.

rationales.rationale: COMED load shows its strongest same‑phase and week‑over‑week positive departures concentrated in the mid window (roughly steps 6–18), indicating the most pronounced upward pressure on price in that span and justifying a strong (++) mid‑window attribution.

System load is moderately above typical levels (horizon mean ~+0.3 sd, end‑to‑end run +0.63 sd) with broadly positive seasonal departure; it warrants a consistent + effect across 1–24 as a secondary contributor.

adjusted.rationale: Judgment fixes a mild positive effect from system_load_fcst across these steps, but the current-window signal is mixed (steps 1–5: system_load ~-1.2 sd, base ~15.21; steps 19–24: system_load ~+0.7 sd, base ~33.63). Treating this as a consistent secondary contributor, I apply a small upward per-step correction of +0.5 to slightly lift the base where supported while keeping the impact modest given the weaker/contrasting early-window system_load.

Judgment assigns a strong ++ upward effect from comed_load_fcst plus a secondary + from system_load_fcst in the mid window. Current mid-window evidence shows comed_load ~+0.9 sd, system_load ~+0.5 sd, and the base ~34.87 (+0.4 sd), indicating substantive upward pressure on price. I therefore apply a larger per-step uplift of +2.5 to reflect the strong combined contribution while keeping the correction proportional to the base scale.

rationales.rationale: COMED load is meaningfully above recent levels (horizon mean ~+0.4 sd and elevated vs the last 24), but the hour‑by‑hour departures vary; a moderate (+) upward effect across the whole window captures the general uplift without asserting an exceptionally large impact.
System load is modestly elevated and seasonally positive (horizon mean ~+0.3 sd, end‑to‑end +0.63 sd), supporting a moderate (+) uplift as a background driver over 1–24.

adjusted.rationale: Both covariates unambiguously push up: COMED is meaningfully elevated (~+0.7 sd) and system load mildly positive (~+0.2 sd). Apply a moderate uniform uplift that captures the general uplift without overstating hour‑to‑hour variability. +4.0 is ~0.29 sd of the target (13.82) and moves the base (≈30.46) upward conservatively across all steps.

rationales.rationale: Although COMED load is above recent levels in parts of the horizon, the positive departures are concentrated mid‑window and show hour‑to‑hour variability versus the cycle; one defensible lower‑risk choice is to leave explicit COMED adjustments out (0) and let other model structure handle localized effects.

PJM system load is consistently elevated relative to recent history (horizon mean ~+0.3 sd, positive seasonal departures), indicating a modest, reliable upward pressure on price that supports a + adjustment across 1–24 as the primary contributor.

adjusted.rationale: System load is consistently elevated across the full 1–24 horizon (roughly +0.2 sd on average, rising to +0.63 sd end-to-end), which supports a modest, uniform upward correction. The base forecast steps average ~30.5, so a small positive nudge of +2.5 per step (roughly an 8% upward adjustment on the current mean) captures the reliable but modest upward pressure without overstating the effect.

PJM system load is moderately elevated (horizon mean ~+0.3 sd, modestly above the recent 24), and same‑phase departures are generally positive; this provides a consistent but smaller upward effect on price, supporting a + adjustment across 1–24.
